extracted.intended_audience: in-house and outside counsel, disclosure committees, investor relations and compliance teams at U.S. public companies with Section 12-registered securities
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for identifying Form 8-K trigger events, preparing and filing timely and compliant Form 8-Ks (including exhibits, tagging, amendments and disclosure controls) for U.S. operating public companies. Emphasizes deadlines, EDGAR mechanics, file vs. furnish distinctions, control processes, and limited SEC relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Deadlines (four business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as described below, a Form 8-K must be filed within four business days after the occurrence of a reportable event. For purposes of counting, day one is the first business day after the day on which the reportable event occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide includes a table showing due dates by weekday (e.g., event on Sunday → due Thursday). Different deadlines may apply for certain items (examples given): Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents — longer reporting period in two limited circumstances: (i) disclosure poses substantial risk to national security or public safety, or (ii) involves customer proprietary network information (CPNI) required to be disclosed under FCC rules); Item 2.02 (earnings announcements — to use the limited exemption for ‘complementary’ earnings calls, the Form 8-K containing the earnings press release must be furnished no later than when the call begins); Item 2.03 (creation of a contingent obligation under certain off-balance sheet arrangements); Item 2.05 (termination of employees as part of a plan to exit an activity); Item 2.06 (material impairments) — in many situations event may instead be reportable in next Form 10-K or Form 10-Q; Item 5.02(c) (appointment of certain new officers) — limited delay may be available; Item 5.04 (temporary suspension of trading under employee benefit plans) — special timing keyed to ERISA notice; Item 5.07(d) (decision regarding frequency of shareholder advisory votes) — longer reporting period; Item 5.08 (shareholder director nominations) — file within four business days after company determines anticipated meeting date. No extension of the Form 8-K due date is available; limited SEC relief exists (see liabilities section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form 10-Q/10-K or Proxy Statement Instead of Form 8-K
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Form 8-K triggering event occurs within four business days before the company's filing of a Form 10-Q or Form 10-K, the company is generally allowed to satisfy its Form 8-K obligation by including the disclosure in the periodic report (Item 5 of Part II of Form 10-Q or Item 9B of Form 10-K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Items 4.01 (Changes in Registrant’s Certifying Accountant) and 4.02 (Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements...) always require a Form 8-K. Forms 10-Q and 10-K cannot be used to report an amendment to a previously filed Form 8-K (amendments must be on Form 8-K/A). General Instruction B.3: timely disclosure in a proxy statement can also satisfy the Form 8-K requirement (except Items 4.01 and 4.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: EDGAR and Public Dissemination Mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: All Form 8-Ks must be submitted via the SEC’s EDGAR system (absent a hardship exemption). Documents submitted via EDGAR become publicly available within seconds of acceptance and online services will send immediate alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDGAR accepts submissions Monday–Friday 6 a.m.–10 p.m. ET (except federal holidays); Form 8-K submissions must be commenced by 5:30 p.m. ET to be considered filed on the date submitted; submissions commenced after 5:30 p.m. ET are considered filed on the next business day. Consider submitting outside market trading hours and coordinate with investor relations. A company with late filing due to technical difficulties can request an adjusted filing date under Rule 13(b) of Regulation S-T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock Exchange Requirements and Advance Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must follow the applicable rules of the exchange where their securities are listed, which generally require advance notice of disclosures of material information (including via Form 8-K). General Instruction E requires that a copy of the Form 8-K be filed with each domestic exchange where registrant’s securities are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Form 8-K filed via EDGAR, NYSE and Nasdaq are deemed satisfied; paper copies only if not filed via EDGAR. Nasdaq rules: Nasdaq Marketplace Rule 5250 and IM-5250-1; NYSE: Listed Company Manual Section 202.06. Only domestic exchanges are included in the instruction. The Guide notes which Form 8-K items may be furnished rather than filed (only Item 2.02 and Item 7.01 may be furnished per the Guide), which affects exchange obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filed vs. Furnished Distinction (liability and incorporation consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some circumstances information 'furnished' to the SEC (rather than 'filed') will be relieved from certain liability provisions and will not be automatically incorporated by reference into registration statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information that is furnished: (1) not subject to Section 18 of the Exchange Act; (2) not automatically incorporated by reference into registration statements; (3) not subject to certain non-GAAP measure prohibitions in Item 10(e) (though other portions may still apply for Item 2.02). The SEC clarified that if a Form 8-K contains disclosures under Item 2.02 or Item 7.01, all exhibits relating to those items will be deemed furnished and relieved from the liabilities unless company designates otherwise. Even where furnishing is allowed, filing may be advisable to enable incorporation by reference into registration statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Requirements and Checkboxes (including use to satisfy Rules 425/14a-12(b)/14d-2(b)/13e-4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover page must include exchange-listed securities information in a specified tabular format and two EGC check boxes. When filing an M&A-related agreement or in connection with proxy or tender offer communications, the company should check the appropriate box on the cover page to indicate the Form 8-K satisfies obligations under Rule 425, Rule 14a-12(b), Rule 14d-2(b), or Rule 13e-4(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking the box eliminates need for separate filing under those Rules if the Form 8-K includes the substantive information required by those other rules. EDGAR requires the Form 8-K to include disclosure under specified items (chart provided) to permit use of the boxes. The boxes are not available when the Form 8-K includes only furnished items. When used properly EDGAR treats the submission as two separate submissions with separate accession numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Tagging and Inline XBRL (Exhibits 101 & 104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are required to tag each data field on the Form 8-K cover page and submit a Cover Page Interactive Data File using an Inline XBRL Document Set with Exhibit 101 attachments. The Cover Page Interactive Data File is identified as Exhibit 104 in the exhibit list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Form 8-K contains no exhibits other than Exhibits 101 and 104, the company is not required to include Exhibits 101 and 104 on the Item 9.01 exhibit list but must still submit the Cover Page Interactive Data File. Cross-reference language should be used (e.g., 'Cover Page Interactive Data File (formatted as Inline XBRL and contained in Exhibit 101)'). See the Interactive Data Files rubric for other tagging requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Under Multiple Items
rubrics_metrics.description: A single event often triggers obligations under more than one Form 8-K item; a single Form 8-K should identify by item number and caption all applicable items being satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Item 1.01 heading may be omitted in a Form 8-K that also includes disclosure under any other item, so long as substantive Item 1.01 disclosure is included elsewhere. All necessary disclosures required by each applicable item must be provided. Examples: hiring a new CEO may require reporting under Items 3.02, 5.02(d), 5.02(c), and 5.02(e); an acquisition may trigger Items 1.01, 2.03, 3.02, and later Item 2.01 and 9.01 disclosures. Care must be taken to ensure completeness for each item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit Requirements (which items require exhibits and schedules guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, copies of agreements underlying a reportable event do not need to be filed as exhibits to Form 8-K, except for specific items that call for exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items calling for exhibits include: Item 1.03 (plan of reorganization/arrangement/liquidation), Item 2.01 (in certain completed acquisition circumstances — financial statements, pro forma, plan of acquisition/disposition), Item 2.02 (furnishing the text of any public announcement or release disclosing material non-public information about results), Item 4.01 and 4.02 (correspondence from auditors), Item 5.02 (certain director correspondence when resigning/removed/refuse to stand), Item 5.03 (text of amendments to charter or bylaws). Under Item 601(a)(5) of Regulation S-K, schedules and attachments may be omitted if they do not contain material information to investment/voting decisions and not otherwise disclosed; omitted schedules must be briefly identified unless already identified in the exhibit. The SEC encourages filing definitive material agreements when feasible. Guidance on 'Titan' language (disclaimer language often used with exhibits that contain reps & warranties) is provided, but the Guide warns disclaimers may not insulate from liability. All exhibits listed must include active hyperlinks in the exhibit index (other than Cover Page Interactive Data File).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titan Language (disclaimer guidance for exhibits)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an exhibit includes representations and warranties, evaluate significance and possible need for additional disclosure so that representations do not convey materially false or misleading information; many companies include 'Titan' disclaimer language when filing M&A agreements as exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample Titan language is provided warning that the agreement is attached only to provide terms, that reps/warranties were made for contract purposes and may be qualified by confidential disclosure schedules, and that investors should not rely on them as characterizations of factual state. The Guide notes the SEC staff has indicated disclaimers without corrective disclosure will not insulate a company from liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Data Files (other than Cover Page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies required to file interactive data files under Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(101) need only file an interactive data file with a Form 8-K if the Form 8-K contains (1) disclosure of a material cybersecurity incident under Item 1.05 (tagging requirement commencing Dec 18, 2024), or (2) audited annual financial statements that are a revised version of previously filed financial statements reflecting specified subsequent events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may voluntarily submit interactive data files with other Form 8-Ks that include financial statements. A Form 8-K cannot be used to correct an initial failure to file an interactive data file on another form; the company must file an amended version of the initial form. Refer to Cover Page Tagging for cover page requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA Safe Harbor for Forward-Looking Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Form 8-K includes forward-looking statements, the company should include appropriate safe harbor language under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tailored PSLRA safe-harbor legends where applicable to preserve protections for forward-looking statements contained in Form 8-Ks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Requirements and CEO/CFO Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K is signed on behalf of the company by any authorized officer. Form 8-K is not required to include the CEO and CFO certifications mandated by Section 302 or Section 906 of Sarbanes-Oxley Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the certifications are not required on Form 8-K, a company’s disclosure controls and procedures must address preparation and filing of Form 8-Ks, and the CEO/CFO certifications included in Forms 10-K and 10-Q regarding effectiveness of disclosure controls must take Form 8-K handling into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Form 8-K (Form 8-K/A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Form 8-K items expressly contemplate a subsequent amendment of the original filing; amendments are filed as Form 8-K/A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items that contemplate amendment include: Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents) — if information required isn't determined at initial filing; Item 2.05 (cost estimates); Item 2.06 (material impairments); Item 4.02 (to file auditor letter if not included initially); Item 5.02(a) (to file departing director's letter); Items 5.02(c) and (d) (if info about new officers/directors unavailable initially); Item 5.07(b) (to report final voting results if preliminary reported earlier); Item 5.07(d) (disclose decision re frequency of advisory votes); Item 9.01 (to file required financial statements and pro forma for certain acquisitions). Amendments must be sequentially numbered, set forth complete text of each item as amended, be signed by an authorized officer, and it's helpful to include explanatory note explaining purpose (especially to correct errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material Cybersecurity Incidents (Item 1.05) — special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1.05 requires disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents; in limited circumstances longer reporting periods apply (national security/public safety risks or CPNI issues). If a company previously disclosed the incident voluntarily under Item 7.01 or 8.01 and later determines the incident is material, the company must file a new Form 8-K under Item 1.05 within four business days of making its materiality determination and include all Item 1.05 disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1.05 contemplates amendments if material aspects of nature, scope, timing, or material impact are not available at initial filing. Companies should develop frameworks for assessing materiality of cybersecurity incidents and align incident response and disclosure controls accordingly (see Impact on Controls rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K Reportable Events (item list and safe-harbor/eligibility mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide lists all Form 8-K reportable events (Items 1.01–1.05; 2.01–2.06; 3.01–3.03; 4.01–4.02; 5.01–5.08; Section 6 ABS items; Item 7.01 Regulation FD; Item 8.01 Other Events; Item 9.01 Financial Statements and Exhibits) and indicates which items have the benefit of the limited safe harbor from Section 10(b)/Rule 10b-5 for failure to file and the impact on Form S-3 eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table shows for each item whether §10(b)/Rule10b-5 safe harbor applies and whether the item affects Form S-3 eligibility; certain ABS items are not addressed by the Guide. The Guide also notes SEC staff interpretation that items should be applied to the company and its subsidiaries unless otherwise clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on Controls and Procedures (disclosure controls must cover Form 8-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public companies must maintain disclosure controls and procedures designed to ensure required information is recorded, processed, summarized and reported in SEC-required time periods; these controls must encompass information required on Form 8-K and be designed to ensure timely reporting of 8-K reportable events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice recommendations (summary): (1) Identify who is most likely to first become aware of each triggering event and educate them; (2) Educate the board about 8-K triggering events and ensure directors communicate actions that may trigger 8-K filings; (3) Pay special attention to resignations and officer/director changes — consider director written-notice policies; (4) Have an effective Disclosure Committee (consider a responsive subcommittee); (5) Ensure multiple people learn about a triggering event (avoid single-point-of-failure); (6) Consider in advance quantitative 'rules of thumb' for materiality (but remember materiality is facts-and-circumstances); (7) Track all unregistered sales of securities; (8) Review policy regarding authorized signatories and require legal review for potentially material contracts; (9) Carefully prepare minutes to distinguish discussion vs. definitive action; (10) Update 10-K/10-Q processes to capture any missed 8-K events and reassess prior materiality determinations; (11) Update cybersecurity controls and incident response plans to conform with Item 1.05 timing and disclosure requirements and document processes for multi-stakeholder communications; (12) Document disclosure controls and procedures after implementing process changes. These steps are recommended to ensure timely 8-K disclosure and to demonstrate effective controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liabilities and Limited Relief (antifraud rules and limited safe harbor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K disclosures are subject to general antifraud provisions (Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5) and Rule 12b-20's requirement that disclosures include all material information to avoid being misleading. Exchange Act Rules 13a-11 and 15d-11 provide a limited safe harbor from Section 10(b)/Rule 10b-5 for a failure to file timely a Form 8-K for certain items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe-harbor applies only to failure to file (not to material misstatements/omissions). Safe-harbor items listed include: 1.01, 1.02, 1.05, 2.03, 2.04, 2.05, 2.06, 4.02(a) (limited), 5.02(e), and 6.03 (ABS). The safe harbor extends only until the due date of the company's periodic report for the relevant period. Failure to timely disclose in the periodic report as a cure will subject the company to potential liability. Failure to timely file many Form 8-Ks typically results in loss of Form S-3 eligibility for 12 months, but late filings for certain items (1.01,1.02,1.04,1.05,2.02,2.03,2.04,2.05,2.06,4.02(a),5.02(e)) do not cause loss of Form S-3 eligibility; waivers are possible in limited circumstances. Rule 144 'current public information' condition is discussed; SEC retains enforcement authority and companies should not rely solely on the limited safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.01 — Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement (detailed rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-K is required if the company has entered into a 'material definitive agreement' not made in the ordinary course of business, entered into any amendment of such a material definitive agreement not in the ordinary course if material, or succeeds as a party to such an agreement by assumption or assignment (other than in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'material definitive agreement' means an agreement providing obligations material to and enforceable against the company, or rights material to the company and enforceable by the company. The determination whether an agreement is 'not made in the ordinary course of business' generally uses Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(10) material contract standards. Compensatory plans/contracts for directors/executive officers and certain equity plans adopted without stockholder approval are not considered 'material definitive agreements' for Item 1.01 (they may be required under Item 5.02(e)). Applying Item 601(b)(10) standards: examples of 'not in the ordinary course' include where the company's business is substantially dependent on the agreement; the agreement calls for acquisition/sale of property/plant/equipment exceeding 15% of consolidated fixed assets; a material lease of property; or where a director/officer is a party (with some exceptions). The Guide provides practice tips and examples of persons likely to first know about such agreements (useful for controls).
